26:Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of Next sprint, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a story at the end of Next sprint, open, its title focused, in the mode last picked for a story. However a story is added, it goes into Next sprint, at its end: a new story, a duplicate, and one added from an Ask answer's card with "Add to sprint" alike. It can then be moved to the Backlog to wait, as the sprint says. The one exception is an accepted proposal for a new story, from drafting, research, or an Ask answer's proposal card, which goes into the Backlog, at its end, as the proposal cards say, and reaches a sprint only once it is moved to Next sprint. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as its prompt.
27:A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), to break it into stories, each with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.
28-
29-## Sprint
30-
--
34:A story can't be sent on its own. The only way a story reaches work is through the sprint: a story in the Backlog waits until it is moved into Next sprint and the sprint is sent, and a story in Next sprint goes when the sprint does. Nothing in Planning, its rows, their menus, the open story, the keyboard, the palette, or the ribbon, sends a single story, and nothing elsewhere sends a story by any other route: a story can't be dragged or copied into the chat input or the queue to be sent from there, and its menu has no "Send" or "Edit in chat input". The chat input's own prompts are not stories and are sent as ever; once a prompt is a story, the sprint is its only way to work. To send one story at once, it is the only story in Next sprint when Send sprint is pressed. A story that failed or was cancelled is sent again the same way, with the next sprint.
35-Sending the sprint moves its stories into a "Current sprint" section, above Next sprint, shown only while it holds a story, so Next sprint is empty again and stories added meanwhile go there, to be the sprint after. A story in Current sprint keeps its place, its row showing its task's status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited there. Once every story of Current sprint has ended, the section offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done into a muted, collapsed "Done" list beneath the Backlog, and those that failed, were cancelled, or stopped to the start of Next sprint, in their order, to be sent again. While a sprint is current, Send sprint is disabled, its tooltip saying a sprint is already under way.
36-Send sprint only ever moves into Current sprint the stories it actually sent. A story with nothing to send, its title and its prompt both empty, is skipped: it stays in Next sprint, where it was, and Send sprint's result says, muted, how many it skipped and why, as "1 empty story left in Next sprint". A sprint where every story is empty sends nothing and makes no Current sprint.
37-Once a sprint is done, it can always be closed. Every story of Current sprint counts as ended once its task has ended, done, failed, cancelled, or stopped, or once its task can no longer be found, as when its record was deleted, it was never recorded, or the application quit before it was. A story whose task is missing is never shown as Queued, or as anything still to come: its row reads "Task missing", muted, in the theme's warning colour, its tooltip saying its task can't be found, and it counts as ended and not Done. A story still waiting in its lane's queue, or held for review, as the paused section says, is still to come and hasn't ended. So Close sprint shows as soon as no story of Current sprint is building, compiling, running, paused, queued, or held, and never waits on a task that can't arrive.
--
63:From top to bottom, Planning reads: the pause bar, while paused; Current sprint, while a sprint is under way; Next sprint; Backlog; Findings; and Done, collapsed. Each is a section headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use the same three parts, below.

65-## Parts
66-
--
69:- A panel: an inset area 16 pixels below what opened it, on the theme's raised surface, corners rounded 6 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, a heading row of 32 pixels with its name, as "Draft stories", "Research", or the story's title, and its close button, its content beneath, and its actions in a footer row, right-aligned, the primary action last; used for an open story, drafting, and research
70-- A card: a box inside a panel, on the theme's base surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 4 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, 8 pixels from the next; a label row at its top, its content, and a footer row of labelled buttons; used for proposals and for each finding's summary
71-Labels are words, never icons alone: every button reads what it does, "Accept", "Send sprint", "Start automatically", and an icon beside a label only repeats it. Each heading's count is a plain number, muted, and each status a coloured label, as the states say. The pause bar is a row across the column's top, 40 pixels tall, its text and buttons on one line, the same height whatever it says.
72-
--
77:- Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
78-- Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
79-- Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
80-A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Paused, or, where its task can't be found, Task missing, as the sprint says, and a story not yet sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".
--
85:- Proposals: loading, the drafting line and spinner; empty, "No stories proposed." with "Draft again"; error, the run's failure with "Try again"; a proposal with no spec cited, in the warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says

87:## Drafting
88-
89:Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
90:Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than the Backlog's heading.
91-The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires while focus is in the box.

93-## Proposals
--
122:Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.
123-Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

125-## Research

127:The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.
128-Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

137:## Keyboard
138-
139:Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. The code already did almost all of this. I made one fix and added tests, but I couldn't compile or run anything, so none of it is verified.

**Already in place:** `src/planning.rs` already catches Enter in the drafting request box, under either label, and starts the draft. Ctrl+Enter starts it too, and the Draft button's tooltip already says "(Enter)". An empty or whitespace-only request starts nothing, and a run already going blocks a second one. Enter in the box stops there, so the list's Enter (open/close story) never fires.

**What I changed:**
- **Shift check:** whether Shift is held now comes from the Enter key event itself, not from the window's current modifier state. So Shift+Enter always adds a new line and never sends.
- **Tests:** I extended `enter_in_the_request_box_starts_the_draft` to check that Shift+Enter adds a new line and sends nothing, that Enter during a run starts no second one, and that Ctrl+Enter starts a draft.

**Not run:** `cargo test` fails before compiling any code. The build embeds files from `.suspense/system-prompts/` and gets "Permission denied" on them, inside the sandbox and out. Once those files are readable, `cargo test enter_in_the_request_box` will check the change.

The spec and the prompt agree here. The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791820081-EnterSubmitsTheDraftStoriesRequest4.understanding.md`.
